## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Security — Operational

Assesses how the target handles errors and exceptional conditions, what and how it logs, how it stores and
delivers secrets, and whether production configuration is locked down, using local, pinned summaries of OWASP and
vendor guidance.

#### Inputs

Global error handlers and exception middleware, logging code and logging configuration, secrets/config loading
code and configuration files (`appsettings*.json`, `web.config`, `application*.properties|yml`, `settings*.py`,
committed `.env` files), container and orchestrator definitions, admin/audit code paths and transaction code, per
`compliance-inventory`.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/owasp-operational.md` — ERR-01…06, LOG-01…26, SMG-01…12, SCR-01…03, A09-01…08,
  A10-01…07. Always load.
- `references/standards/dotnet-operational.md` — DNO-01…16. Load when language `csharp` is detected.
- `references/standards/java-operational.md` — JVO-01…06. Load when language `java` is detected.
- `references/standards/python-operational.md` — PYO-01…09. Load when language `python` is detected.
- `references/standards/node-operational.md` — NDO-01…05. Load when language `javascript` is detected.
- Framework elements apply only when that framework is in use; runtime and library elements apply whenever the
  language is detected. Container, orchestrator and CI files are evaluated with the language-agnostic SMG and LOG
  elements whenever they are in the subject's files.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill, and never use remembered defaults: an error-page, logging or
  secret-store default counts only when a localized element states it. Do not load
  `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, the standards files that apply (above), and
   `references/languages/<id>.md` for each detected language (detection signals only; they cite no standard).
2. Read as the Secure Code Review method suggests (scr#review-process, scr#data-flow-analysis): start from the
   global error handler, logging configuration and configuration loading, then trace high-risk paths (admin
   functions, data export, authorization decisions, multi-step writes) to their error paths and log calls. The
   method guides reading; it is not scored.
3. For each check SEC-OP-01…SEC-OP-10, evaluate the elements it lists against the subject's files, using the
   signal files to find evidence. Mark a check N/A with a reason when no element applies (e.g. SEC-OP-07 when no
   production configuration is in the files; SEC-OP-10 when there are no multi-step writes or security
   decisions in the files).
4. **Secret candidates.** When the payload has `secretCandidates` (file, line, rule, confidence from the step-01
   pattern pass and, with `--advanced`, `gitleaks`; never the value), read each candidate line with ±3 lines of
   context, even when the file isn't in your own list, and decide whether it is a placeholder or a real secret.
   Real secrets fail SEC-OP-05, with `confidence: high` for a format match (`aws-access-key-id`, `github-token`,
   `private-key-block`, `gitleaks:*`, …) that the context confirms and `medium` otherwise. A name-only candidate
   (a key file or keystore, `line: null`) fails SMG-02 when the file is in the repository. When
   `secretCandidatesTotal` is larger than the list, add `secret-candidates-truncated: <total>` to `notes`.
5. Evidence rules: fail an element only on concrete code or configuration in the files (see the evidence notes in
   `checklist.md`). A missing setting counts only when a localized element states the insecure default; for
   libraries without one, add `localized-standard-gap: <library> default for <setting> not localized` to `notes`.
   Platform-injected environment variables are acceptable secret delivery; SMG-07 and DNO-11 never fail on their
   own. Don't fail on speculation. Use confidence `medium` unless the evidence is unambiguous.
6. Ownership: management-endpoint network placement is judged here (ORS-01 under SEC-OP-07). Don't report
   authentication/authorization/session-failure logging or management-endpoint authorization (identity-access), SQL injection in log writes (input-injection), HTTP headers (web-api),
   telemetry attributes, correlation IDs, audit/diagnostic log separation or health-endpoint detail
   (observability), alerting, SIEM routing, retention or telemetry-store access (monitoring), general robustness
   outside security paths (software-quality), rate limits and quotas (reliability), library versions
   (dependency-management), error-response format (api-design) or personal-data storage, exposure, sharing and test
   data (review-data-protection). Logging rejected input verbatim is judged here.
7. Severity: MUST/REVIEW elements take the check's default from `checklist.md`; SHOULD elements one level lower
   (Error → Warning, Warning → Information). Always Error, whatever the check's default: production debug mode,
   developer exception page or stack-trace/message exposure (PYO-01 `DEBUG = True` in production settings; DNO-06
   `UseDeveloperExceptionPage()` not gated on Development; JVO-01 `include-stacktrace`/`include-message` =
   `always`), and Actuator `env`/`configprops` exposed over HTTP with `show-values: always` (JVO-03). When several
   elements fail on the same evidence, write one finding at the highest severity. `checkResults.severityIfFailed`
   is the check's default.
8. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `LOG-01`); the report script derives `standard` and `url`
   from it, so don't write them. Prefer a vendor element, then a cheat-sheet element, then an A09/A10 element (cite
   A09/A10 only when nothing more specific fits; otherwise name the Top 10 ID in the recommendation). For an element
   marked (Default), cite the OWASP element it supports and name the vendor element in the recommendation. Where
   vendor guidance is weaker than an OWASP element, the OWASP element decides.
9. If the reference date (date part of `startedAt`) is more than 9 months after a standards file's "Localized"
   date, add `localized-standard-stale: <file> localized <date>` to `notes`.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

Totals: 48 OWASP cheat-sheet + 15 Top 10 + 16 DNO + 6 JVO + 9 PYO + 5 NDO = 99 elements across 10 checks.

#### Evidence notes

- **SEC-OP-01 / SEC-OP-07:** fail on code or configuration that returns exception messages, stack traces, SQL errors
  or paths to clients, or that enables detailed error output for production. Configuration gated on a development
  environment or profile passes.
- **SEC-OP-07 (ORS-01):** fail only when the files show management or diagnostic endpoints (Actuator, admin, metrics,
  debug routes) served on the public listener with no separate port or host and no network restriction (ingress
  allowlist, firewall rule, bind address) in the files in scope; confidence `low` when the deployment network isn't in
  scope. Their authorization stays with identity-access.
- **SEC-OP-02:** fail on catch blocks that neither log, rethrow nor translate the exception (empty or comment-only
  catch, bare `except: pass`), or on a handler that marks an exception handled without logging where a localized
  default says nothing else logs it (DNO-10, PYO-05).
- **SEC-OP-03:** fail when a log call or logging configuration writes a value that is a secret or sensitive personal
  data (variables or properties named like password/secret/token/apiKey/connectionString/cardNumber,
  `Authorization`/`Cookie` headers, whole request or entity objects known to contain them), or enables body/header
  logging of such data. The finding's excerpt names the logged field but never shows a logged value
  (`<redacted:kind>`; see "Redaction" in `finding-schema.md`).
- **SEC-OP-05:** fail on literal credential values in source or configuration files in the repository: keys named like
  password/secret/api_key/token/connectionString with a non-placeholder value; private-key blocks; recognizable cloud
  key formats; `.env` files with values present in the repository; plain Kubernetes `Secret` manifests with data. Placeholders (`${…}`,
  `<secret>`, `changeme`-style samples clearly marked as such), password-less local development connection strings and
  files outside the subject's list don't fail, except the lines named in the payload's `secretCandidates`, which the
  worker reads wherever they are (`../SKILL.md` step 4). Use confidence `medium` unless the value is unambiguous.
  Coverage includes CI workflow files (literal values in `env:` blocks or `run:` steps), Dockerfile `ARG`/`ENV`
  defaults, notebook outputs, and package-manager auth files (`.npmrc` `_authToken`, `.pypirc`, Maven
  `settings.xml` `<password>`, `NuGet.config` `ClearTextPassword`), judged with SMG-02/SMG-03; where no element fits a
  case, add `localized-standard-gap` to `notes` instead of failing. **Redaction:** the excerpt keeps the key name and
  replaces the value with `<redacted:kind>` (e.g. `"ApiKey": "<redacted:api-key>"`); `validate` rejects an excerpt that
  still contains a secret.
- **SEC-OP-06:** secrets injected as environment variables by the platform or orchestrator at deploy time pass.
  SMG-07 and DNO-11 never fail on their own; name them in recommendations only. Environment-variable values hardcoded
  in container or compose definitions in the repository fail SMG-02 (SEC-OP-05).
- **SEC-OP-08:** fail only when the subject's files contain the security-relevant operation itself (e.g. a
  user-administration endpoint, a data export, a deserializer, a startup routine) and no logging call covers it, or
  when security-relevant code writes events with `print`/`Console.WriteLine`/`System.out` instead of the logging
  framework. Authentication, authorization and session-failure logging is not evaluated here.
- **SEC-OP-09:** evaluate only what application code and configuration show (log paths, file appenders,
  rotation/size settings, log endpoints, transport URLs, logging-config loading). Log storage access control in IaC
  belongs to `review-monitoring`.
- **SEC-OP-10:** fail on catch blocks in authorization, authentication, validation or limit checks that allow or
  continue (fail open); multi-step writes without a transaction or rollback on exception; streams, connections or
  locks not released on exception paths (no `using`/try-with-resources/`with`/`finally`).

## File: `references/standards/owasp-operational.md`

*Load rule: ERR-01…06, LOG-01…26, SMG-01…12, SCR-01…03, A09-01…08, A10-01…07. Always load.*

### OWASP operational security guidance — localized summary

- Level: `MUST` where the source says must/must not/never/do not/ensure, gives an unqualified imperative, or names a
  prohibited practice; items of the Logging sheet's "Where possible, always log" list are `MUST`. `SHOULD` for
  recommendations (should/recommended/prefer/consider/"if available"). Secure Code Review checklist items are `MUST`.
  Top 10 elements: `MUST` for "How to prevent" bullets, `REVIEW` for "Description" weaknesses and mapped CWEs (`REVIEW`
  is treated like `MUST`). Severity rules are in `../../SKILL.md`.
- Untrusted data: anything the application didn't create — request parameters, bodies, headers, cookies, file names,
  queue messages, partner feeds and data from other trust zones.
- Language-agnostic files (`Dockerfile`, compose files, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, pipeline YAML) have no
  language id. Evaluate them with the SMG and LOG elements below whenever they are in the subject's file list.

#### Error Handling Cheat Sheet (ERR)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ERR-01 | MUST | Configure a global error handler (runtime configuration or code) so every unexpected error is caught centrally. | no `UseExceptionHandler`, `@RestControllerAdvice`/`<error-page>`, `handler500`; per-action try/catch only | SEC-OP-01 |
| ERR-02 | MUST | On unexpected errors return a generic response; no stack trace, exception message, framework/server version, SQL error or file path in the body or headers. | `ex.ToString()`/`e.getMessage()`/`str(e)`/`traceback` in responses | SEC-OP-01 |
| ERR-03 | MUST | Log the error details server-side for investigation in the handler, instead of returning them. | handler builds a response but never logs the exception | SEC-OP-02 |
| ERR-04 | MUST | Detailed or developer error pages are enabled only for development; other environments use the generic handler (`customErrors` `RemoteOnly`/`On`, never `Off`). | `UseDeveloperExceptionPage()` ungated; `customErrors mode="Off"` | SEC-OP-07 |
| ERR-05 | MUST | Java web apps declare a catch-all `<error-page>` for `java.lang.Exception`/`Throwable`, or a Spring `@RestControllerAdvice` with `@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)`, returning a generic body. | no catch-all error page or advice | SEC-OP-01 |
| ERR-06 | MUST | ASP.NET Web API (.NET Framework) registers a global `IExceptionLogger` and `IExceptionHandler` that returns a generic response. | `WebApiConfig` without both services replaced | SEC-OP-01 |

#### Logging Cheat Sheet (LOG)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LOG-01 | MUST | Log input validation failures (protocol violations, bad encodings, invalid parameter names/values, values outside a discrete list) and output validation failures. | validation rejects requests with no log call | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-02 | MUST | Log application errors and system events: runtime errors, connectivity problems, third-party service errors, file system errors, upload virus detection, configuration changes. | catch of I/O/HTTP-client errors without logging | SEC-OP-02 |
| LOG-03 | MUST | Log application start-up and shut-down, and logging initialization (start, stop, pause). | no startup/shutdown log in host code | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-04 | MUST | Log use of higher-risk functionality: user administration and privilege changes, administrator actions, default/shared/break-glass accounts, sensitive-data access, key use/rotation, data import/export, uploads. | admin/user-management/export endpoints with no logging | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-05 | MUST | Log deserialization failures, network connection failures (including backend TLS and certificate-validation failures) and requests with unexpected HTTP verbs. | swallowed deserialization/TLS exceptions | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-06 | MUST | Log legal and other opt-ins: consent to personal-data use, terms of use, marketing permissions. | consent endpoints with no event logged | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-07 | MUST | Log suspicious business-logic activity: out-of-order steps, actions that make no business sense, attempts to exceed limits. | limit/state checks reject silently | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-08 | MUST | Each security event records when (timestamp, international format), where (app/version, host, service, entry point and method, code location), who (source address, user identity) and what (type, severity, description). | security log calls with message text only | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-09 | SHOULD | Security events also record action, object, result status and reason (and HTTP status for web apps). | "failed" with no object or reason | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-10 | MUST | Never exclude events from "known" users or systems (internal services, monitors, testers); flag them instead. | log filters that skip internal IPs or service accounts | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-11 | MUST | Use the framework's logging mechanism or one application-wide log handler for security events, not ad-hoc writes. | `print`, `Console.WriteLine`, `System.out` for security events | SEC-OP-08 |
| LOG-12 | MUST | Don't log session IDs (hash if needed), access tokens, authentication passwords, database connection strings, encryption keys or other primary secrets; remove, mask, hash or encrypt them. | token/password/connection-string values in log arguments; whole request/header objects logged | SEC-OP-03 |
| LOG-13 | MUST | Don't log sensitive personal data (health, government IDs), bank or card-holder data, application source code, commercially sensitive data, data above the log store's classification, or data the user didn't consent to. | logging full user/payment entities | SEC-OP-03 |
| LOG-14 | SHOULD | Treat file paths, internal network names and addresses, and non-sensitive personal data (names, phone numbers, emails) specially: mask, pseudonymize or omit where identity isn't needed. | emails/phone numbers logged on every request | SEC-OP-03 |
| LOG-15 | MUST | Treat event data from other trust zones as untrusted: validate it before logging; omit or safely replace malformed fields and record the failure, without discarding the event. | partner/queue payloads logged raw | SEC-OP-04 |
| LOG-16 | MUST | Neutralize log injection: strip or encode CR, LF and delimiter characters in untrusted data, or write values through a structured (e.g. JSON) encoder that escapes them. | user input in text-format logs with no CR/LF handling | SEC-OP-04 |
| LOG-17 | MUST | Keep message templates constant and pass untrusted values as parameters; never concatenate them into the template (parameterization alone doesn't stop CR/LF). | `logger.warn("user " + name + " {}", x)`; interpolated templates | SEC-OP-04 |
| LOG-18 | MUST | Encode logged data correctly for the log's output format (e.g. safe for HTML log viewers). | logs rendered in a web UI without encoding | SEC-OP-04 |
| LOG-19 | MUST | The default log level gives enough detail; application logging, and logging of compliance-required events, can't be fully deactivated; level changes follow approved configuration or change control. | production `LogLevel: None`/`OFF` for app or security loggers; runtime toggles without control | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-20 | MUST | Failures in logging don't stop the application or leak information. | logging calls that can throw into request handling | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-21 | MUST | Logging can't be used to exhaust resources: bound the size of user input in log messages and cap file growth (rotation, size, history). | file appenders without rotation/size caps; unbounded user strings logged | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-22 | SHOULD | Logs aren't stored in web-accessible locations; if unavoidable, access is restricted and they're served as plain text. | log path under `wwwroot`/`static`/`public`; log-file endpoints | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-23 | SHOULD | File logs use strict directory and file permissions (ideally a separate partition); database logging uses a separate, write-only account. | world-writable log dirs (`chmod 777`); app DB account used for logs | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-24 | MUST | Log data sent over untrusted networks uses a secure transport. | `udp://` syslog, `http://` log collector endpoints | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-25 | MUST | Logs are protected from tampering and unauthorized access, modification and deletion; read access is restricted. | app endpoints that read, edit or delete logs without authorization | SEC-OP-09 |
| LOG-26 | SHOULD | Build in tamper detection and copy logs to read-only storage as soon as possible. | audit logs in mutable app tables only | SEC-OP-09 |

#### Secrets Management Cheat Sheet (SMG)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMG-01 | MUST | No hardcoded secrets in plaintext in source, configuration files or configuration-management tooling: API keys, database credentials, private keys, certificates, tokens. | literal credentials; committed `.env` with values; PEM blocks; start from `password\s*=\|api_key\s*=\|secret\s*=` | SEC-OP-05 |
| SMG-02 | MUST | Secrets aren't built into container images: no secrets in Dockerfile `ENV`/`ARG` or copied secret files; the orchestrator mounts or injects them at runtime. | `ENV DB_PASSWORD=…`; `ARG API_KEY=…`; `COPY secrets.json`; literal values in compose `environment:` | SEC-OP-05 |
| SMG-03 | SHOULD | Encryption keys aren't stored next to the secrets they encrypt, unless they are themselves encrypted (envelope encryption). | encrypted config value and its key in the same file | SEC-OP-05 |
| SMG-04 | SHOULD | Secrets committed to Git (GitOps) are asymmetrically encrypted with environment-specific keys (e.g. Sealed Secrets). | plain Kubernetes `kind: Secret` manifests with `data`/`stringData` | SEC-OP-05 |
| SMG-05 | SHOULD | Secret detection runs before commit or PR (pre-commit hook, IDE or CI scanner). | no secret scanner in hook/CI files in scope | SEC-OP-05 |
| SMG-06 | SHOULD | Use a designated secrets manager, not a general-purpose configuration store; ideally the deployed service fetches its own secrets at runtime with its platform identity, so secrets don't pass through CI/CD. | secrets in parameter/config stores; pipeline writes secrets into config | SEC-OP-06 |
| SMG-07 | SHOULD | Environment variables carry secrets only when file mounts or in-memory fetch aren't possible, and are set by the orchestrator, never hardcoded. **Advisory only; never fails on its own.** | — (recommendation text) | SEC-OP-06 |
| SMG-08 | SHOULD | Production and development secrets are separate, ideally in separate secret stores with reduced access to production. | same secret values in dev and prod config | SEC-OP-06 |
| SMG-09 | SHOULD | Access to secrets is least-privilege and scoped per application and environment; no account-wide access; no secrets shared across services. | one credential reused by several services; wildcard secret permissions | SEC-OP-06 |
| SMG-10 | SHOULD | Prefer dynamic, short-lived credentials or workload identity; static secrets support rotation, expiry and revocation, and the app verifies a secret is still active. | long-lived keys where managed identity exists; secrets read once and cached forever | SEC-OP-06 |
| SMG-11 | MUST | Never transmit secrets in plaintext; secret-store and credential exchanges use TLS. | `http://` vault address; TLS verification disabled for the secret store | SEC-OP-06 |
| SMG-12 | SHOULD | CI/CD tooling holds no high-value, long-lived secrets; pipelines authenticate with OIDC/workload identity federation and short-lived, least-privilege credentials. | static cloud keys in pipeline variables or YAML | SEC-OP-06 |

#### Secure Code Review Cheat Sheet (SCR)

The review method (scr#review-process, scr#data-flow-analysis) is procedure guidance in `../../SKILL.md`, not scored.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCR-01 | MUST | Secure defaults: shipped and default configuration is security-focused (debug off, diagnostics off, least exposure). | production config inherits development settings | SEC-OP-07 |
| SCR-02 | MUST | Environment separation: configuration and settings are isolated per environment; development settings aren't deployed to production. | single settings file with dev values; dev profile active by default | SEC-OP-07 |
| SCR-03 | MUST | Transaction atomicity: multi-step operations have proper rollback and consistency mechanisms. | multi-write operations without a transaction | SEC-OP-10 |

#### REST Security Cheat Sheet — management endpoints (ORS)

Prefix `ORS-` (operational REST) keeps these IDs apart from `review-security-web-api`'s `RST-` elements, which cite
other sections of the same sheet under that skill's budget.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ORS-01 | MUST | Management and diagnostic endpoints aren't exposed to the internet: they listen on a separate port or host (preferably a restricted network) or are restricted by firewall rules or access lists; if they must be internet-facing, they require strong (multi-factor) authentication. | Actuator/admin/metrics endpoints on the public listener with no `management.server.port`/address, ingress or IP restriction in the files | SEC-OP-07 |

#### OWASP Top 10:2025 A09 Security Logging & Alerting Failures (A09)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A09-01 | MUST | Login, access-control and server-side input validation failures can be logged with enough user context, and kept long enough for forensics. (Login/access-control logging is judged by identity-access.) | — | SEC-OP-08 |
| A09-02 | MUST | Every part of the app that contains a security control is logged, whether it succeeds or fails. | — | SEC-OP-08 |
| A09-03 | MUST | Logs are generated in a format that log-management solutions can consume. | — | SEC-OP-08 |
| A09-04 | MUST | Log data is encoded correctly to prevent injection into logging or monitoring systems. | — | SEC-OP-04 |
| A09-05 | MUST | Transactions have an audit trail with integrity controls against tampering or deletion (append-only tables or similar). | — | SEC-OP-09 |
| A09-06 | MUST | Transactions that throw an error are rolled back and started over; always fail closed. | — | SEC-OP-10 |
| A09-07 | REVIEW | Sensitive information (PII, PHI) is logged, or logging/alerting events are visible to users. | — | SEC-OP-03 |
| A09-08 | REVIEW | Warnings and errors produce no, inadequate or unclear log messages, or errors are mishandled so the system is unaware of them. | — | SEC-OP-02 |

#### OWASP Top 10:2025 A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions (A10)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A10-01 | MUST | A global exception handler catches anything missed; exceptional conditions are handled in one place, the same way each time. | — | SEC-OP-01 |
| A10-02 | MUST | Catch errors where they occur and handle them meaningfully: inform the user understandably, log the event, alert if justified. | — | SEC-OP-10 |
| A10-03 | MUST | Roll back every part of a part-way transaction and start again (fail closed); don't try to recover mid-transaction. | — | SEC-OP-10 |
| A10-04 | REVIEW | Error messages or debug code expose sensitive information (CWE-209, CWE-215, CWE-550). | — | SEC-OP-01 |
| A10-05 | REVIEW | The application fails open (CWE-636) or mishandles insufficient privileges (CWE-274, CWE-280). | — | SEC-OP-10 |
| A10-06 | REVIEW | Resources aren't cleaned up when an exception is thrown (CWE-460), e.g. locked after failed uploads. | — | SEC-OP-10 |
| A10-07 | REVIEW | Errors are detected without action, return values or error conditions go unchecked, or generic catches hide failures (CWE-252, CWE-390, CWE-391, CWE-396). | — | SEC-OP-02 |
